cases.title: Human Profile Isolation
cases.situation: Two Humans use the same PlotPickle Node and must remain separate private users.
cases.businessReason: PlotPickle is multi-user on one physical machine; switching profiles is a security boundary, not a cosmetic preference.

humanJourney.action: Unlock Human A.
Create or observe Human A private state.
Lock/switch and unlock Human B.
Attempt to reach Human A private state from Human B.
Restart/switch again and verify isolation remains intact.

preconditions: A test Node can host two isolated Human profiles.
Test data is non-sensitive and reversible.
cases.expectedOutcome: Human B cannot see or use Human A projects, vault data, BUZZ identity, credentials, private UI state or retrieval context before or after restart.

requiredEvidence.description: Human A private state exists in profile A.
Human B session is authenticated as profile B.
Attempted cross-profile access is denied or absent.
Isolation remains correct after restart/profile switch.

independentVerification.proves: The second Human session cannot observe the first Human's private state.

knownRisks: project storage mounted under wrong profile
injectedFailureModes: restart with previous Human state cached
authorityBoundaries: No destructive edits to real Human data.
Use test-scoped profiles for fault injection.

cases.title: Connect Existing BUZZ Identity
cases.situation: A Human already owns a BUZZ private identity and chooses Connect Existing Identity from Profile.
cases.businessReason: Community identity must belong to the Human and must work through the real profile flow before Community can be trusted.

humanJourney.action: Open BUZZ Identity in the authenticated Human profile.
Choose Connect Existing Identity and provide a test-scoped existing identity.
Verify the derived public signer independently.
Persist connected state to the authenticated Human.
Open the built-in PlotPickle Community using that identity.

preconditions: A non-production BUZZ test identity is available.
cases.expectedOutcome: PlotPickle accepts a valid existing BUZZ identity, rejects invalid identities, binds the verified signer only to the authenticated Human, persists Connected state and can enter the built-in Community.

requiredEvidence.description: Safe interaction trace shows the real profile connection flow without exposing the private key.
Independent verifier confirms the expected public signer.
Connected state survives the required persistence boundary.
The built-in Community opens and recognizes the connected Human identity.

independentVerification.proves: The connected public signer matches the expected test identity and is usable by Community.

authorityBoundaries: Never store a private BUZZ key in Casebook evidence.
BUZZ is not PlotPickle login authority.
Identity is scoped to the authenticated Human.

cases.title: Great Hall Signed Conversation
cases.situation: A connected Human posts a normal message in the PlotPickle Great Hall.
cases.businessReason: Community is a core product capability; a locally rendered message is not enough unless the same signed BUZZ event exists and is read back through the shared history.

humanJourney.action: Open Great Hall as the connected Human.
Send a unique test-scoped message.
Observe the signed BUZZ event independently.
Read the same event back into PlotPickle.
Reload/restart as required and confirm the same event remains reconciled.

preconditions: A connected BUZZ test identity exists.
The test Human can enter the Great Hall.
cases.expectedOutcome: A message sent from PlotPickle is represented by one independently observed signed BUZZ event, is read back into PlotPickle using the same event identity and remains consistent after reload/restart.

requiredEvidence.description: Human-visible Great Hall send state.
Independent signed BUZZ event identifier.
PlotPickle read-back references the same event identity.
Reload/restart does not create a competing local message record.

independentVerification.proves: The Great Hall message exists as the expected signed BUZZ event outside the sender's own UI assertion.

injectedFailureModes: publish accepted locally but read-back unavailable
authorityBoundaries: Do not post private project material.
Do not treat optimistic local UI as authoritative BUZZ proof.
successCriteria: One signed event is independently observed.
Human-visible conversation remains consistent after reload.

cases.title: Local Text AI / Sage Usable Response
cases.situation: A Human asks Sage a reasonable question about the current LEARN lesson while a local text route is selected.
cases.businessReason: Sage is a curriculum guide; a provider HTTP success or non-empty string is insufficient if the Human receives nonsense, vague fallback text or the wrong lesson context.

humanJourney.action: Open a known LEARN lesson.
Ask Sage a clear lesson-grounded question.
Route through the selected local text provider.
Render Sage's Human-facing answer.
Evaluate relevance, usability and provider-failure semantics.

preconditions: A supported local text runtime/model is configured or an intentional unavailable-state test is selected.
cases.expectedOutcome: Sage returns a concise, relevant curriculum-grounded answer through the selected provider, or an explicit actionable provider/runtime error; vague internal fallback text never counts as success.

requiredEvidence.description: Human question and lesson reference are identified.
Selected local provider/model route is observed.
The actual answer shown to the Human is captured safely.
Independent evaluator classifies the answer as usable/relevant or correctly errors.

independentVerification.proves: The Human-visible Sage response is usable and grounded in the current lesson, not merely non-empty.

knownRisks: runtime unavailable but UI pretends success
authorityBoundaries: Provider output is advisory and must not silently change story canon.
Do not expose hidden model reasoning.
successCriteria: Human-visible answer is useful or explicit actionable error is shown.

cases.title: Local ComfyUI Image Generation Visible in PlotPickle
cases.situation: A Human configures local ComfyUI and runs a PlotPickle image test on a Windows machine.
cases.businessReason: Image generation is only successful when the configured local service is genuinely usable and the generated asset is visibly returned to PlotPickle; service health or job completion alone is not the Human outcome.

humanJourney.action: Choose Configure ComfyUI.
Detect/launch or connect to the configured local ComfyUI service.
Verify model, VAE/checkpoint and workflow-node prerequisites.
Submit a real local test image generation.
Independently verify the generated output asset exists.
Retrieve and visibly render the same asset in PlotPickle.
Mark Ollama + ComfyUI Local selectable only after the required proof is complete.

preconditions: Windows real-machine mode is available for full integration proof.
ComfyUI may be installed or absent; the Case must distinguish those states.
cases.expectedOutcome: PlotPickle accurately detects/starts or connects to local ComfyUI, verifies complete prerequisites, generates a real test image, independently proves the output exists, displays that image to the Human and enables the local route only after proof is complete.

requiredEvidence.description: Configured local endpoint health and process/service state.
Required model/checkpoint/VAE/workflow nodes are verified.
Real test generation job/output identity.
Independent observer confirms the output asset exists.
The generated image is visibly rendered in PlotPickle.
The local route is selectable only after complete proof.

independentVerification.proves: The generation produced a real local asset that PlotPickle retrieved and displayed, independently of the submitter's success claim.

knownRisks: job says complete but output absent
output exists but UI does not display
authorityBoundaries: Local route only; no silent paid-cloud fallback.
Do not download/install large models without explicit approval.
successCriteria: Real generated asset is independently observed.
The same image is Human-visible in PlotPickle.
Local route readiness matches the proven state.
